# Memento - Platform Specification

Version 1.0 - 2026-10-28 - Selected React frontend, Bun backend, SQLite/PostgreSQL adapters and Podman development profile.

Read [Product](memento-spec.md), [Experience](memento-experience-spec.md), [Domain](memento-domain-spec.md) and [Technical](memento-technical-spec.md) for the behaviour and contracts realized here. This document selects implementation technologies and boundaries. Selection is not evidence that the application, dependency compatibility, performance or deployment gates have passed.

## 1. Adopted platform decisions

The user authorizes the frontend technology baseline in [spikes/02-react-renderer-comparison/package.json](../spikes/02-react-renderer-comparison/package.json), a backend running on Bun, SQLite for normal development/tests, PostgreSQL for deployment, and Podman development containers. These replace the earlier Rust/Axum/Tokio/SQLx platform and the previous mandatory Tailwind/shadcn/React Router/ELK selections.

The spike manifest and its lockfile are implementation references, not the product's semantic model or production package. Its renderer can inform the application, while its mock backend and experimental data representations require replacement by the specified domain/application use cases. The third collaboration spike and its OpenSpec/Yjs proposal retain experimental scope; they do not override the platform or select CRDT merging for Memento.

| Concern | Selected baseline |
| --- | --- |
| Browser | React and React DOM with TypeScript, client-rendered. |
| Board | React Flow (`@xyflow/react`) with owned custom cards/controllers and SVG/DOM presentation. |
| Drawing | `perfect-freehand` for stroke outline generation, mapped to board-owned durable ink. |
| Icons/font | `lucide-react`; locally bundled `@fontsource/ibm-plex-sans`. |
| Styling | Repository-owned CSS/theme tokens/components, following the mockup and renderer spike. No additional CSS framework is required by the selected manifest. |
| Build/dependency tooling | Bun package manager/scripts and committed lockfile; Vite build/dev server with React plugin; explicit TypeScript checking. |
| Backend | TypeScript on Bun; `Bun.serve` HTTP and WebSocket adapter, application composition and durable workers. No Node or Rust server process is required. |
| SQLite implementation | Separate repository/unit-of-work adapter using `bun:sqlite`, normal test/development default. |
| PostgreSQL implementation | Separate repository/unit-of-work adapter using Bun SQL, mandatory deployment store and real parity-test target. |
| Tests/lint | Vitest and Playwright for frontend/component/browser coverage; Bun test for backend/domain and adapter suites; oxlint and TypeScript checking. |
| Development containers | Podman, Containerfiles and OCI images, retained named/bind volumes and loopback ports. |

The backend's initial toolchain pin is Bun 1.4.0, the locally available version inspected on 2026-10-28. Validate application/driver compatibility at bootstrap; changing the pin is recorded with lockfile/build/parity evidence. This is not a measured deployment certification.

## 2. Frontend dependency baseline

The following are declared manifest versions/ranges, not claims about every transitive resolved package. Preserve the spike lockfile as the experiment's evidence; the application gets its own committed lockfile and license inventory. Reconcile compatible changes explicitly rather than silently selecting latest versions.

| Runtime dependency | Declared version |
| --- | --- |
| `react`, `react-dom` | 19.3.1 |
| `@xyflow/react` | 12.12.0 |
| `lucide-react` | 1.60.0 |
| `perfect-freehand` | 1.2.3 |
| `@fontsource/ibm-plex-sans` | 5.3.0 |

| Development dependency | Declared version/range |
| --- | --- |
| `typescript` | ~6.0.3 |
| `vite` | ^8.3.4 |
| `@vitejs/plugin-react` | ^6.1.2 |
| `vitest` | 5.0.5 |
| `@playwright/test` | 1.64.1 |
| `oxlint` | ^1.88.0 |
| `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom` | ^19.3.0 |
| `@types/node` | ^24.19.2; tooling declarations do not select a Node backend. |

Bun-specific backend type declarations are selected/pinned compatibly during bootstrap. No database ORM, additional server framework or model SDK is selected solely by this manifest. The baseline uses native server/driver adapters behind context interfaces; introduce another dependency only for a defined responsibility and with notices/compatibility evidence. All mandatory application components remain open source; hosted proprietary collaboration is not a dependency. Model endpoint/weight licensing is a separate deployment decision.

## 3. DDD code organization and dependency rules

The following is the target layout, not a claim that directories already implement the product:

```text
apps/
  web/src/                 # shell, features, board adapter, API client
  server/src/              # Bun entry, HTTP/WS, composition, worker entry
packages/
  memento/src/
    workspace-access/
    collaborative-knowledge/
    visual-collaboration/
    agent-participation/
    connected-work/
  contracts/               # public request/result/event schemas and client types
  storage/src/
    sqlite/
    postgres/
migrations/
  sqlite/
  postgres/
deploy/
  app/                     # application Containerfile/run profile when implemented
  test-environment/        # existing independent service package
```

Domain code uses plain validated TypeScript values and deterministic operations; it does not import Bun server requests, React/React Flow node types, SQL rows or provider SDK messages. Application use cases establish authorization, transaction and orchestration boundaries. HTTP, storage, model, connector, password/session and clock/ID facilities are adapters. Use small explicit ports only where an external concern exists, without a generic repository/service for every value object.

Context exports expose the Domain Specification's command/query interfaces. Enforce dependencies through TypeScript project/package boundaries and import checks. A consumer cannot import another context's private persistence mapping. Cross-context transactions are coordinated at application composition through a shared unit of work and each owner's published interface. Shared types contain IDs/references/operation metadata, not one mutable universal entity.

The two database adapters share repository contracts and contract tests. The application does not branch its business rules on the selected engine. Internal table names may be context-prefixed, but transport and model tools use published DTOs. Runtime schema validation is required even when browser/server share TypeScript types.

## 4. Browser application and design system

Vite builds static assets; Bun serves those assets and APIs under one deployment origin, or an explicitly configured reverse proxy does. Development Vite proxies API/WebSocket traffic to Bun. The app owns route/URL parsing and navigation contracts for Access, Home, workspace/Board, Templates and global/board Activity. A specific routing library is not mandated by the referenced package; add one only through an explicit dependency decision.

Feature modules cover access/members, Home/return state, templates, composition/inspection, Sources/publication, Agents, Activity and Traceability. A shared UI layer owns controls and theme tokens. Ordinary CSS variables define surface/text/border/accent/paper palettes, spacing, typography, focus, depth and responsive behavior. Reuse Node shell, reference-information card, status badge, contextual action, modal, form error and toast patterns. Match the Experience Specification's information/action distinction and canonical panel/drawer/dialog behavior.

Import the selected font locally through the build; browser runtime must not rely on a remote font CDN. Lucide icons provide consistent control symbols with accessible names; decorative icons do not replace labels. `perfect-freehand` produces rendering geometry for recorded strokes; the persisted source points/style/identity are owned by the composition model, not an opaque library cache. Measure stroke/card density with actual intended rich content.

Keep authoritative server state, pending local interaction, personal durable markers and ephemeral view state separate. Favorites/visits/read markers persist per member through the server. Theme/view/selection/open-panel preferences can remain browser-local; they grant no authority. Content, Decisions, conversations, captured evidence and outcomes cannot rely on localStorage for durability. Optimistic state stays visibly pending until accepted; conflicts preserve the draft.

## 5. React Flow as a presentation adapter

Map node IDs to Placement/VisualElement representations with explicit domain references and revisions. A source projection includes the selected ObservationId; it cannot subscribe directly to a global latest source value. Removing a renderer node invokes RemovePlacement, not DeleteRecord. Note colour belongs to visual presentation and never increments content evidence revision.

Custom nodes support freeform inline Notes, captured sources/tasks, Proposals, Decisions, Actions, Text and Shape. Gestures inside editable text/buttons must not trigger canvas pan/drag. Frame membership is explicit and batches member arrangement through validated commands; geometric overlap alone does not assign permanent membership. `perfect-freehand` and SVG render ink/link paths in the same board coordinate system.

A handle drag creates a visual link only. Semantic supports/origin, Decision supersession, results-in and Action prerequisite use the contextual domain commands and are labelled/inspected as semantic records. Traceability is a composed information dialog/query, not a second React Flow document or required ELK layout. The platform does not require automatic layout or CRDT merely because the library can display graphs.

Internal collaboration follows Technical section 3: server-accepted HTTP operations, ordered committed WebSocket updates, explicit stale-write conflicts and recoverable snapshots. Yjs/Yrs are not selected for production. A later proposal must define exactly which fields merge and preserve authority, provenance and acknowledgement before changing this contract. Visual undo sends a new revision-aware operation; it cannot invoke knowledge/external reversal.

## 6. Dual storage and backend runtime

Choose storage explicitly at composition time. Public use cases are asynchronous; the SQLite unit-of-work implementation executes synchronous statement/transaction work without `await` inside `bun:sqlite` transaction bodies. The PostgreSQL implementation awaits queries through the same transaction connection. They implement Technical section 4's protected authority/graph reads, constraints, deduplication, publication and durable work rules.

| Configuration | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `MEMENTO_PROFILE=development` | Defaults to SQLite and a retained writable file; Bun native development or the Podman app image is supported. |
| `MEMENTO_PROFILE=test` | Isolated SQLite by default; shared adapter suites explicitly select PostgreSQL as an additional real-engine target. |
| `MEMENTO_PROFILE=deployment` | Requires PostgreSQL and valid deployment secrets/origin settings; never silently starts with SQLite. |
| `MEMENTO_STORAGE=sqlite` | Uses the resolved `MEMENTO_SQLITE_PATH`, including the development/test default; open flags/permissions and required pragmas are checked at readiness. |
| `MEMENTO_STORAGE=postgres` | Requires `MEMENTO_DATABASE_URL`; pool/timeout/SSL configuration is explicit and credentials are not logged. |
| Invalid profile/driver/settings | Startup/readiness fails with safe diagnostics rather than changing storage or creating an accidental empty database. |

The intended default development path is `./var/memento.sqlite`, ignored by Git. Container profile mounts the containing directory at `/data`, covering database/WAL/SHM files; its path becomes `/data/memento.sqlite`. In-memory SQLite is useful for isolated tests, not restart or realistic concurrency evidence. Enable foreign keys per connection and use WAL/FULL durability for file profiles. PostgreSQL version/image is pinned when its deployment/parity profile is authored; the existing Nextcloud PostgreSQL 17 package is not automatically Memento's selected database instance.

Migrations have paired logical versions and engine-specific statements as required. Use transaction-scoped repositories, explicit conversion/validation and shared contract tests. SQL is parameterized; dynamic identifiers come from fixed validated mappings. Do not assume SQLite type affinity, PostgreSQL JSON operators, collation or transaction timing are interchangeable. Adapter-specific locking may differ, while tested business outcomes must agree.

Bun handles HTTP/WS and asynchronous inference/provider I/O. Avoid CPU-heavy synchronous hashing or long database scans on the main loop; apply bounded payloads and use asynchronous facilities/workers where measured need requires them. Bun native WebSocket publication is a transport optimization, not a durable outbox. Background work is database-backed, versioned and safely resumable.

## 7. Agent and connector integration

Model and provider adapters translate external APIs into Domain interfaces. Provider SDK types never become aggregate state. A runtime records actual supplied messages, ContextSelection and granted tools; every tool invokes authorized application use cases. Credentials remain server-held. Select the model provider/client during its implementation change and record actual inference evidence and operating configuration.

| Concern | Selected service / scope |
| --- | --- |
| Local mail | Stalwart Community, accessed by the validated adapter protocol; Nextcloud Mail is the independent participant client. |
| Tasks | Nextcloud Deck, with explicit native assignee/due/completion mapping and actual create/reconcile evidence. |
| Independent chat/files | Nextcloud Talk/Files remain external environment clients, not general Memento connectors. |
| Source reads | Scoped on-demand browse/import/refresh/publication; no always-running record synchronization. |
| Writes | Exact reviewed create-task/send-reply Actions, with durable identity and uncertainty recovery. |

Endpoint/account values in the mockups are illustrative. The [Test Environment](../test-environment.md) defines actual local ports/accounts, native service versions, startup/reset and independent client checks. Application connector configuration references those settings explicitly. Provider outage changes operation availability, not historical evidence. Recovery and Action reconciliation must not become an unrequested background refresh of unrelated source records.

## 8. Podman containers and operating profiles

Use a Containerfile to build an OCI application image with Podman; no Docker daemon is required in development. The target build command shape is `podman build --format oci -f deploy/app/Containerfile -t localhost/memento:<version> .`; the Containerfile and executable runbook are implementation deliverables, not files created by this specification rewrite.

The image contains a pinned Bun runtime, server application and built browser assets. Build with locked dependencies, type-check explicitly and retain required notices. Runtime uses an unprivileged user, explicit writable data path and health/readiness endpoints. Keep secrets in ignored/private configuration or runtime secret injection, never in the image/repository. Native packaging/compilation is optional only after measured compatibility evidence; the basic runtime deployment is sufficient.

Normal local application runs retain SQLite in a named/bind volume and publish only a documented loopback port. Real external services remain in their existing separate supervised container. Real PostgreSQL parity testing uses a separately named database/container and isolated data; it does not write Nextcloud's database. Deployment uses PostgreSQL with controlled migrations/backups; a deployment orchestrator is not selected by the Podman-development decision.

Podman start/stop/recreate checks cover permission to write the volume, SQLite sidecars/consistent restart, readiness, worker/outbox recovery and static/API same-origin behavior. Record macOS host/Podman VM architecture and image digest; successful ARM64 operation is not Intel/Linux acceptance. Existing service evidence remains dated and bounded; updating a documented media-format command does not retroactively validate a rebuilt image.

## 9. Verification, pinning and decisions

Run domain/use-case tests without HTTP, renderer, model or external provider dependencies. Run shared persistence suites against both real engines. Type-check both frontend and backend separately from Vite transpilation. Verify public schemas/client mapping, dependency boundaries and actual browser journeys; run real provider/inference/deployment profiles for their respective ACs. Test selection and evidence belong to the authorized slice, not a blanket claim from a build.

The initial product scripts should provide check/typecheck/lint/test/build/migrate/seed/start and both adapter-test targets when implementation introduces executable tooling. Their exact commands are recorded then; the specification does not claim scripts already exist. Frontend Vitest and backend Bun test have different responsibilities. Tests of Node-based experimental spikes remain separate from Bun application acceptance.

Remaining implementation choices are the exact locked application dependency graph, backend type declarations, migration runner, provider/model adapters, PostgreSQL deployment version, credential storage integration and measured host/browser/graph budgets. Their change designs must preserve R/S stories, DR rules and Technical AC gates. No open technology choice permits silently restoring Rust, continuous external sync, renderer-owned semantics or PostgreSQL-only development.

## 3. Product structure expressed by the mockups

The design is an application around a collaborative board, with these connected journeys:

| Journey | Visible path and intended result |
| --- | --- |
| Account entry | Entry → My account → email/password → Home → an authorized workspace and board. |
| Invitation entry | Entry → I have an invitation → workspace/inviter/Editor preview → display name and code/link → access limited to the invited workspace. |
| Start work | Home → New workspace → name and initial access → first empty board; alternatively Templates → Use template → named workspace and editable first board. |
| Resume work | Home → owned/shared filter or search → workspace/board preview → recent/favorite board → inspect changes and continue. |
| Think and organize | Board → notes, text, shapes, frames, ink, visual links, selection and arrangement → inspect or edit material. |
| Bring evidence | Sources → configured, scoped service → browse/select record → import capture → inspect, annotate, open original, inspect history or manually refresh. |
| Ask AI | Select material → attach it to Agents chat → choose Facilitator or Action Coordinator → send request, answer clarification, inspect result or cancel. |
| Decide and act | Inspector/context menu → optional Proposal or direct Decision → preserve rationale/evidence → prepare an Action → review exact operation → approve → execute → inspect outcome. |
| Recover the reason | Inspector or Activity → Traceability → pinned evidence/details/history → locate an existing placement or deliberately show a retained record on the board. |

These paths are product requirements to specify and implement. Navigation currently ending in a toast, browser-local storage, a preview or a scripted outcome is incomplete mockup behaviour, not the target implementation.

## 5. External references: the corrected contract

### 5.1 What “static evidence” means

A Connection lets an authorized participant request an interaction with an external service. It does not maintain a continuously changing mirror of that service on the board. The external system owns its native email/task; Memento owns the captured observation and the knowledge built around it.

| Situation | Required Memento behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| A participant imports a message or task | Capture the selected external content and metadata as an immutable Source Observation; create/reuse its Source Record identity and explicitly place the chosen capture where requested. |
| The external task changes or is completed | The imported card remains at its captured state until a participant requests refresh. Do not silently update status, content, relationships, AI context or Decisions. |
| A new email arrives | It does not automatically appear on the board. A participant can browse the configured scope and import it. |
| The user opens the original | Navigate to/locate the external record. The external service applies that viewer's own authorization; viewing it does not refresh Memento. |
| A participant manually refreshes | Recheck current authority and source scope; fetch on demand; preserve previous captures; record who requested it, when, and the result. A changed capture becomes a new observation, never an overwrite. |
| The provider reports no content change | Record the refresh check/result without inventing a semantic content change. Deduplication may reuse the existing capture/fingerprint. |
| Refresh fails, access is revoked or the native record is gone | Preserve existing evidence and annotations. Report that the requested refresh failed/unavailable; do not replace the capture with empty content or imply it is now current. |
| The connection recovers or the application restarts | Restore Memento state and operation status. Recovery alone does not refresh imported references. |
| A real approved Action creates a task or delivers a reply | Record the returned/confirmed result and external identity. This is a specific operation outcome. Further native changes still require requested refresh. |

Internal collaboration remains live: when Maya deliberately imports or refreshes material, Leo can receive the resulting committed **Memento** update. This is not continuous synchronization with the external provider. Likewise, presence and agent progress can use WebSockets without changing this external-evidence rule.

### 5.2 Identity, history and display consequences

The existing Source Record / immutable Source Observation / Evidence Reference distinction is a strong foundation and should be retained. The amendment must tighten its consumers:

- Source Record identifies the native record through its original Connection/source identity. It can index observations, but a global “latest observation” pointer must not silently advance every card or evidence reference.
- A displayed imported reference needs an explicit observation reference. **Derived design contract:** record which capture a Placement/view presents, and change it only through the user's refresh/selection operation. If a refresh can update several placements, that scope must be explicit. It cannot quietly update unrelated boards.
- Evidence References on Decisions and Agent Runs continue to pin exact revisions. Refresh does not retarget existing evidence or retrospectively add the new data to a run.
- Local annotations, card geometry, frame membership and semantic relationships survive refresh. Their authorship and revisions remain independent of provider content.
- A pending Proposal may become stale when newer evidence is deliberately introduced or its actual referenced working context changes. An unseen external edit cannot trigger a freshness claim. A recorded Decision keeps its original meaning and evidence; a human may reassess/supersede it.
- Display “Captured at …”, “Observed status at capture …”, “Last refresh attempt …” and “Refresh source”. Connection availability, capture age and external business status are separate fields. Avoid “Live”, “Up to date” or “Synced” where only an old capture is known.
- Provider credentials remain server-side. Members may read published workspace evidence under workspace authorization, while opening the original and requesting refresh can require separate provider capability. Personal-source publication policy remains explicitly unresolved under CM-22.

For example: import a Deck task while it is Open; complete it in Deck; the Memento capture still says Open with its capture time. Press Refresh source; a new observation says Completed. A Decision recorded against the original Open observation still opens that original revision. Merely reconnecting or revisiting the board performs none of these refresh steps.

### 5.3 Contradictory mockup controls and labels

| --- | --- |
| Sources: “New arrivals: place automatically”; configuration checkbox for automatic placement | Replace with explicit browse/import behaviour. Do not carry an automatic-arrival toggle into the corrected connector contract. |
| “Simulate scoped arrival” | Demo machinery; if retained, demonstrate a record becoming available for participant selection, not unrequested board mutation. |
| Actors such as “Email sync”, “Task sync”, “Mail sync”, “Deck sync” | Attribute to the importing member and connector capture/refresh operation. System-origin normalization remains attributable, but the copy must not imply a standing synchronization service. |
| Timeline “Task status updated” and demo step “Leo completes the task in Deck” | Include the explicit requested refresh before a new captured status appears. The provider edit and the Memento capture are different events. |
| “Reading resumes after recovery” | The connection becomes available for new requested operations. Existing captures remain unchanged until requested refresh. |
| Connection-level “Last checked” | Describe the connection/operation check, separately from each reference's captured version and time. |
| Inspect original / Refresh source / Observation history | Keep these separate controls: original navigation, deliberate capture update, and historical evidence inspection. |

### 5.4 Connector and worker consequences

T4.1's compulsory incremental retrieval/polling cursor becomes an on-demand browse/import/refresh contract. Pagination or bounded retrieval may still be used inside a requested browse/refresh; it does not imply scheduled monitoring. Stable provider IDs, locators, normalized fields, fingerprints, permission checks, error classification and import deduplication remain required.

Durable jobs remain useful for a requested refresh, model inference, approved external execution and uncertain-outcome recovery. They must record the initiating command and its scope. The static-evidence rule removes the product's need for a continuing external synchronization worker; it does not remove the internal committed-update outbox or the duty to establish the outcome of an already submitted Action.

Stalwart and Nextcloud Mail/Deck remain the selected local services. Their real-read/write/client checks still matter. No new mail, task, chat or document provider is selected by the mockups. Nextcloud Talk/Files availability remains independent of Memento connectors; the personal-email sharing prototype adds no general file/attachment integration.

Rename/archive/delete and retained-evidence consequences are not designed comprehensively. |
| Template definitions | Six structures are promised by previews. Define exact seeded content, versioning and instantiation; decide whether user-authored templates are supported. The design does not show a template authoring product. |
| Capture refresh scope | No continuous synchronization is settled. Specify how a user selects which displayed references advance during one requested refresh and whether batch refresh is exposed; historical pinned evidence always stays fixed. |
| Personal-source publication | The guided prototype makes audience/provenance and separate original authorization clear. Confirm release inclusion, who can refresh a published capture, redaction/withdrawal and evidence-retention rules. Its prototype status is not completed product policy. |
| Retained-material search | Board search filters displayed material; Traceability exposes unplaced records. Define a usable search route for retained knowledge so removing a placement never makes required history undiscoverable. |
| Conversation scope/retention | Board chat is visible. Define who can see a conversation, whether multiple threads exist and retention; do not assume private or workspace-global chat from the panel alone. |
| Operational profile | Model provider, measured host/browser support, connector protocols/reconciliation and renderer reassessment remain open. The mockup resolves none of these by using native JavaScript or sample endpoints. |

There is no need to infer billing, enterprise SSO, public workspaces, calendar operations, general document/attachment connectors or autonomous agents from the visible screens. Those require their own product decisions. The actual visible template/freehand/access journeys, however, must be reconciled with release scope rather than dismissed by obsolete exclusions.

# Open source board libraries for Memento

Research date: 2026-10-15. Audience: front-end engineering and product review. Status: investigation complete; candidate spikes and technology decision pending.

## Recommendation

**Reopen the board choice and test Plait, AntV X6, and Foblex Flow against the same Memento board, with React Flow as the comparison baseline.** Plait is the first candidate for a broad whiteboard; X6 is the first alternative for an application built around rich cards and relationships; Foblex supplies an Angular-native comparison. Give Excalidraw a short feasibility test for interactive cards. Keep BlockSuite conditional on proving compatibility with Memento's collaboration contract. Include a direct HTML/SVG implementation as a credible fallback with an explicit engineering cost.

This is an engineering assessment from upstream documentation and source licences. It does not establish a winner through measured prototypes. None of the reviewed options establishes all of Memento's present and future needs out of the box. Drawing tools, interactive application cards, multiplayer delivery, and domain history are different capabilities; a candidate must demonstrate how they work together.

The [Platform Specification](../memento-platform-spec.md) currently selects React and React Flow. This investigation broadens the comparison to Angular, Svelte, Web Components, framework-independent JavaScript, and native browser rendering. It leaves the selected baseline in place until the spike review. Choosing Angular or another application framework would require an explicit platform amendment after that review. The [spike briefs](../../delivery/releases/v1.0/board-library-spikes.md) are proposed assignments, not implementation authorization.

## Open source eligibility

All required shipped functionality must be buildable and self-hostable from open-source code. Source visibility, a free tier, an educational licence, or a production licence key does not satisfy the requirement. Use the [Open Source Definition](https://opensource.org/osd) as the eligibility reference. Copyleft licences remain eligible; record their actual distribution obligations with the selected packages.

Each spike must inventory the exact package versions, renderer/adapters, plugins, example code, assets, fonts, and any collaboration service it uses. A core repository's licence does not establish the licence of everything in a demo. Keep required capabilities independent of proprietary services. The licence links below describe the inspected upstream trees on the research date; the pinned spike packages still require their own inventory.

Two boundaries are particularly relevant:

- React Flow and Svelte Flow have an [MIT core](https://github.com/xyflow/xyflow). React Flow's [freehand example](https://reactflow.dev/examples/whiteboard/freehand-draw) explicitly uses the xyflow Pro licence. Count freehand as work to implement independently with eligible dependencies; do not count that example as reusable MIT functionality. Other examples must be checked individually.
- The current [tldraw SDK licence](https://tldraw.dev/community/license) requires a production key and explicitly distinguishes the SDK from open-source software. Exclude it from the shortlist. MIT examples do not change the SDK's status. Historical versions are not a substitute for evaluating a maintained dependency.

## Integration requirements that can eliminate a candidate

1. **Keep semantic records outside the editor document.** Map visual IDs to Placement IDs and separate record references. Content and arrangement revisions remain independent; removing a shape must not delete evidence. Rebuild the projection from authoritative records.
2. **Control acceptance.** A gesture produces a local preview and a proposed command. The server accepts or rejects it using expected revisions and operation identity. Rejecting a command must restore the accepted projection without corrupting the editor's local history. An `onChange` notification alone does not prove this is possible.
3. **Separate drawing from meaning.** Decorative arrows and frame membership must not invent semantic Relationships. A generic edge editor cannot freely rewrite Decision supersession. Imported/generated diagrams require explicit mapping and validation.
4. **Preserve rich-card interaction.** Test text selection, editing, scroll, menus, buttons, focus and IME input at multiple zoom levels, with card resize and parent movement. Canvas overlays and SVG `foreignObject` renderers need browser-specific evidence.
5. **Reconcile remote changes.** Preserve an active draft while applying an independent committed move. Show a same-content conflict explicitly. Restore authoritative state after missed updates. BlockSuite's Yjs foundation is an additional boundary to prove, rather than an automatic disqualification for using a CRDT internally.
6. **Own undo and portability.** A committed undo is a fresh revision-aware command. It cannot erase a recorded Decision or reverse external execution. Export must account for fonts, images, DOM overlays, evidence references, and missing assets. Library JSON is an adapter format, not the domain's only durable store.
7. **Measure representative complexity.** Use realistic email text, task metadata, evidence links, forms and connectors. Assess accessibility and pointer/touch behaviour as well as frame rate. An upstream large-node demo with simple boxes cannot establish the supported Memento board size.

## Proposed decision sequence

Use the [common fixture, individual briefs and review gates](../../delivery/releases/v1.0/board-library-spikes.md) to keep the comparison fair.

1. Run the Plait and X6 spikes first. They test the broad-whiteboard and rich-card approaches directly.
2. Run Foblex in Angular and React Flow with the same fixture. If Angular is attractive, briefly compare ngx-vflow before selecting its library.
3. Run short Excalidraw and BlockSuite gates only on their decisive risks. Extend a passing candidate to the common fixture; stop a failing one with a small reproducer.
4. Use the native HTML/SVG fallback if the first candidates cannot reconcile card interactivity, whiteboard breadth, and command control. Consider Konva/Fabric when drawing needs justify a Canvas layer; avoid adding two complete editor engines before measuring the integration cost.
5. Take the best two eligible candidates through the same collaboration, accessibility, portability, and performance exercise. Select by observed coverage and remaining engineering effort. Record the final platform decision and synchronize affected specifications/PDFs at that point.

A credible choice must cover all MVP elements, demonstrate a viable path for every wider element, and state the cost of each gap. If no candidate does this within an acceptable effort, narrow the intended whiteboard scope explicitly or fund a custom surface. A percentage of feature names checked off is insufficient when a missing capability is the interactive card or authoritative-command boundary.

# Memento — UI interaction spike specification

Version 1.0 · 2026-10-20 · Scope: local UI experiment; human acceptance pending.

## Purpose and authority

Demonstrate a small spatial board where a participant can inspect the evidence behind a process, rearrange its elements, navigate the canvas and extend the graph. This specification defines the observable interaction baseline for UI spikes. The [shared scene](../delivery/releases/v1.0/board-scene-proposal.md) supplies the Atlas fixture; the [spike briefs](../delivery/releases/v1.0/board-library-spikes.md) retain the broader comparative experiments.

[`01-basic-html`](../spikes/01-basic-html/README.md) is the bottom-end, native-browser baseline. **It must use no runtime libraries**, frameworks, packages, CDN resources, remote fonts, vendor APIs or hosted services. Implement its UI using repository-owned HTML, CSS, JavaScript and SVG plus built-in browser APIs. It opens directly from `index.html` without installation, compilation, a server or network access. Bun may serve an optional loopback preview; Playwright may verify it as development tooling. Neither is part of the browser runtime. Other candidate spikes must identify their own runtime dependencies.

The [Functional and Domain Specification](memento-spec.md), [Technical Specification](memento-technical-spec.md) and [Platform Specification](memento-platform-spec.md) continue to own product behaviour, collaboration contracts and application technology. This experiment changes none of those contracts or the selected application platform.

## Required behaviour

| ID | Requirement and observable result |
| --- | --- |
| UI-01 Fixture and evidence | Retain nine process shapes, ten process arrows, four Yes/No labels, two post-its, the initial highlighted constraint-review step, its two-comment thread, and two linked evidence conclusion cards. Selecting a step highlights its relevant evidence. Inspect E1's three illustrative messages, E2's three versioned document excerpts, and the two comments. Source content and conclusions remain distinguishable. |
| UI-02 Move elements | Independently move every process shape, post-it and evidence card using a labelled, focusable move handle. Preview movement continuously; retain the dropped position for the page session. Pointer capture completes a drag outside the viewport. Evidence buttons, text selection and typing do not start dragging or panning. Keyboard arrows on a move handle move by 10 board units; Shift+arrow moves by 1. Geometry changes do not change content or evidence associations. |
| UI-03 Navigate | Pan by dragging empty canvas, or with the Hand tool across non-control surfaces. Provide zoom in/out, a 100% control and Fit board, with a visible zoom percentage. Zoom ranges from 20% to 200%; wheel/trackpad zoom is anchored at the pointer. Toolbar zoom is anchored at the viewport centre. Fit computes bounds from all movable elements, including additions and negative positions, down to the 20% zoom limit; larger arrangements remain accessible by panning. Viewport resizing preserves board coordinates. On narrow screens keep the spatial board, tools and inspector usable without page horizontal overflow; zoom/pan supplies access to the whole scene. |
| UI-04 Create and edit | A small Box palette button can be dragged onto the viewport to create a rectangular process box centred at the drop position, accounting for pan and zoom. Clicking or keyboard-activating it creates a box at the viewport centre. Dropping outside creates nothing. Each new box has a stable local ID, can be selected and moved, and has a plain-text editable label in the inspector. Post-it text is also editable there. Saving changes only the selected object's text; blank labels are rejected visibly. Labels accept up to 240 characters and wrap within the fixed card width; content height may grow without changing board position. User text is rendered as text, never HTML. |
| UI-05 Connections | Existing solid process arrows and dashed evidence connections keep their original endpoint IDs and labels while either endpoint moves and while navigating. Provide a Connect tool: choose a process shape as the source and another as the target to add one solid directed arrow. Reject self-links and duplicate directed process links with an explanation. Evidence cards and notes are not valid process endpoints. New arrows are visual fixture connections, not published semantic Relationships. Connection creation exits after success; Escape or selecting another tool cancels it. |
| UI-06 Controls and cancellation | Clearly indicate Select/Hand/Connect mode and the selected object. Escape cancels an active drag, palette drag or connection and restores the pre-gesture state; pointer cancellation does likewise. Escape also closes source/comment details and returns focus to their opener. Source/comment details and the label editor remain outside the transformed world so their controls stay readable at any zoom. Provide Reset board to restore the original elements, text, connections, selection, inspector and fitted viewport. Reload has the same initial-state result. No storage is used. |
| UI-07 Readability and input | Preserve distinct shape families, arrows, evidence line styles, light/dark appearance, visible keyboard focus, meaningful control names and status feedback. Support mouse and single-pointer touch/pen movement, palette creation and panning through Pointer Events. Native buttons supply keyboard activation. At 50%, 100% and 200% zoom, evidence inspection and editing must work without unintended object movement or viewport changes. At 320, 390, 736 and 1440 pixel widths, controls remain reachable; source details wrap/scroll without page overflow. |
| UI-08 Reproducibility | Keep an executable browser check, a dated result with actual tool/browser versions and zero runtime dependencies, and current desktop/mobile/dark/inspection/interaction screenshots. Verify direct file opening with HTTP(S) requests blocked, all UI-01–UI-07 workflows, coordinate conversion at multiple zooms, cancellation, reset and optional loopback HTTP serving. Record unverified environments separately. |

## Implementation boundary

Use one board coordinate system for all movable element geometry and SVG connectors. Separate local object identity/content, placement geometry, visual connections and viewport/selection/tool state. Convert pointer coordinates through the viewport's inverse translation and scale for movement and creation. Derive connector endpoints from current board geometry; avoid grid-specific routing that detaches when elements move. The fixture's frame is a visual guide and does not constrain movement or establish semantic membership.

The local state is experimental, not a substitute for server-accepted commands. Moving a Source Card preserves its illustrative observation and inspection. Spatial proximity, arrows and frame bounds do not record a Decision, establish evidence or perform an external action (DR-03/04). See functional sections 4.7–4.10 and technical sections 2–3 for product integration requirements.

Resizing, grouping, multi-selection, freehand, automatic layout, undo history, deletion tools, persistence, authentication, multiplayer, conflict/reconnect handling, real ingestion, model inference and external writes are outside this increment. This specification covers part of the original V05 manipulation check; its resizing requirement and the full SP-07/C01–C07 experiments remain separate work. No product release AC is completed by this spike.

## Review demonstration

1. Open `index.html` offline; inspect E1, E2 and the review comments.
2. Move the constraint step, a post-it and its evidence card; observe attached arrows and unchanged evidence.
3. Pan, zoom to 50% and 200%, and operate evidence controls; return with Fit board.
4. Drag Box to open space, rename it, and connect an existing process step to it.
5. Move the new box and verify its arrow follows. Exercise keyboard movement and cancellation.
6. Repeat creation at a different zoom/pan, then Reset and reload; the original fixture returns.

Actual verification, screenshots, remaining gaps and human review are recorded in the [baseline README](../spikes/01-basic-html/README.md), [check record](../spikes/01-basic-html/verification.json) and [SP-07 brief](../delivery/releases/v1.0/board-library-spikes.md#sp-07-direct-html-and-svg-fallback). Automated checks and human acceptance remain separate facts.
